subject: radiology
title: Ring Enhancing Lesions: Abscess, Tumour and Tuberculoma

steps.title: Ring enhancement has a short list
steps.tx: **Ring enhancing lesion** on post contrast CT or MRI gathers abscess, necrotic tumour, tuberculoma, resolving haematoma, demyelination and radiation necrosis into one shape. The mnemonic MAGIC DR lists metastasis, abscess, glioblastoma, infarct, contusion, demyelination and radiation change. Wall character, diffusion behaviour and the clinical temperature of the patient sort that list faster than ring size, which correlates with almost nothing.

steps.title: Abscess restricts diffusion
steps.tx: **Brain abscess** fills its cavity with pus that restricts diffusion strongly, bright on diffusion imaging and dark on the ADC map, the single most useful sequence split from necrotic tumour whose watery centre diffuses freely. The pictured abscess routes show haematogenous, sinus and dental sources seeding the corticomedullary junction. A smooth thin capsule, daughter lesions and fever complete the pattern that earns aspiration before antibiotics alone are trusted.

The pictured routes show cardiac, sinus and dental sources seeding the corticomedullary junction. Fever and a smooth thin capsule complete the pattern earning aspiration.

steps.title: Glioblastoma crosses the corpus callosum
steps.tx: **Butterfly glioma** is glioblastoma crossing the corpus callosum into both frontal lobes, an infiltrative growth no capsule contains. Its ring is thick, irregular and nodular with central necrosis, surrounding vasogenic oedema and mass effect out of proportion in an afebrile older patient. Spectroscopy raises choline and drops N acetylaspartate across even the normal looking margin, proving infiltration beyond the ring that surgery can never fully clear.
steps.say: Butterfly glioma is glioblastoma crossing the corpus callosum into both frontal lobes. Its ring is thick, irregular and nodular with central necrosis in an afebrile older patient. Spectroscopy shows infiltration beyond the ring that surgery can never fully clear, separating it from a contained abscess.

steps.title: Tuberculoma and caseous centres
steps.tx: **Tuberculoma** rings a caseous centre that reads T2 dark when solid caseation dominates, unlike the T2 bright necrotic centre of most tumours. Conglomerate rings clustering near the meninges with basal meningitis, infarcts from vasculitis and hydrocephalus complete the tuberculosis picture in endemic settings. Target sign with central calcification inside the ring is the classic late appearance, and steroids ride with antitubercular therapy when paradoxical expansion threatens vision or consciousness.
steps.say: Tuberculoma rings a caseous centre that reads T2 dark when solid caseation dominates, unlike the bright necrotic centre of tumours. Conglomerate rings with basal meningitis and hydrocephalus complete the tuberculosis picture. Steroids ride with antitubercular therapy when paradoxical expansion threatens vision or consciousness.

steps.title: Open ring favours demyelination
steps.tx: **Open ring sign** leaves the enhancing ring incomplete on the cortical side, the gap pointing toward grey matter, and it favours demyelination over abscess or tumour with high specificity. Tumefactive multiple sclerosis builds these large rings with little mass effect for their size and modest oedema. A young patient with prior transient neurological episodes and an open ring earns oligoclonal band testing and spine MRI before any biopsy is booked.

steps.title: Metastases sit at the junction
steps.tx: **Brain metastases** lodge at the grey white junction where vessels narrow, often multiple, round and surrounded by vasogenic oedema far larger than the nodule itself. Lung, breast, melanoma, renal and colon primaries dominate, and melanoma or renal deposits bleed into the ring. A solitary ring in a patient with known cancer is still metastasis only about nine times in ten, so atypical features reopen the abscess and primary tumour possibilities.

steps.title: Toxoplasmosis in advanced HIV
steps.tx: **Toxoplasmosis** rings cluster in basal ganglia and corticomedullary junction when CD4 counts fall under 100, often multiple with an eccentric target nodule inside the ring wall. Lymphoma in the same host hugs the ventricles, crosses the corpus callosum and restricts diffusion from dense cellularity. Two weeks of antitoxoplasma therapy with imaging response is the classic test, because toxoplasmosis shrinks and lymphoma does not.
steps.say: Toxoplasmosis rings cluster in basal ganglia when CD4 counts fall under one hundred, often with an eccentric target nodule in the wall. Lymphoma hugs the ventricles and restricts diffusion from dense cellularity. Two weeks of antitoxoplasma therapy with imaging response is the classic separating test.

steps.title: Radiation necrosis mimics recurrence
steps.tx: **Radiation necrosis** rings appear months to years inside a treated tumour field, copying recurrence on conventional MRI almost perfectly. Perfusion imaging separates them because necrosis has low blood volume while recurrent tumour rebuilds vessels with high blood volume. Spectroscopy and amino acid PET add votes in the same direction. The treatment forks are opposite, steroids and bevacizumab against necrosis versus more tumour therapy, so the imaging distinction is never academic.
